title: Electronic Transactions Proclamation 1205/2020: use of electronic messages not mandatory without consent
claim: The Ethiopian Electronic Transactions Proclamation No. 1205/2020 provides that nothing makes it mandatory for a person to use, provide or accept any electronic message in commercial transactions or dealings with government bodies unless the person consents.
evidence_summary: Article 4 ('Use not Mandatory') of Proclamation No. 1205/2020 provides that nothing shall make it mandatory for a person to use, provide or accept any electronic message in any commercial transaction or dealings with government bodies unless the person consents to it.
source_excerpt: 4. Use not Mandatory Nothing shall make it mandatory for a person to use, provide or accept any electronic message in any commercial transaction or dealings with government bodies unless the person consents to the using, providing or accepting of the electronic message.
interpretation: Normative evidence of a consent/voluntariness principle for electronic transactions in Ethiopia, including dealings with government bodies. Establishes a legal floor against forced digitalization of transactions; does not evidence practice.
citation: Electronic Transactions Proclamation No. 1205/2020, Art. 4 (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 57, 30 June 2020).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from primary legal text (Article 4, Use not Mandatory).
keywords: electronic transactions, consent, mandatory, digital government, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/4/eth_etrans_1205.pdf); locator Article 4.

title: Electronic Transactions Proclamation 1205/2020: legal recognition of electronic messages
claim: The Ethiopian Electronic Transactions Proclamation No. 1205/2020 provides that information shall not be denied legal effect solely on the ground that it is in the form of an electronic message, and treats electronic messages as satisfying writing requirements.
evidence_summary: Proclamation No. 1205/2020 provides legal recognition for electronic messages: information shall not be denied legal effect solely because it is in electronic form, and where the law requires information in writing, that requirement is met by an electronic message containing the information in accessible form.
source_excerpt: Information shall not be denied legal effect solely on the ground that it is in the form of an electronic message... 8. Writing Where the law requires information to be in writing, that requirement is met by an electronic message if the information contained in it is accessible.
interpretation: Normative evidence that Ethiopia's e-transactions framework grants legal effect to electronic messages, underpinning the legal layer of digital public infrastructure. Establishes legal recognition; does not evidence deployment.
citation: Electronic Transactions Proclamation No. 1205/2020, legal recognition and writing provisions (Federal Negarit Gazette No. 57, 30 June 2020).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quotes from primary legal text (legal effect; writing).
keywords: electronic transactions, legal recognition, writing, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/4/eth_etrans_1205.pdf).
